page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard.E4.128 is a bare-metal server powered by AMD EPYC 7J13 processors built on the x86_64 architecture. The platform delivers 128 physical cores operating at 2.55 GHz and scales to 256 vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading with dedicated CPU allocation. It is configured with 2048.0 GB of memory, establishing a high ratio of 8.0 GB of system RAM per virtual processor.

The bare-metal implementation eliminates virtualization layers and hypervisor overhead, ensuring predictable execution latency and full control over CPU and memory subsystems. BM.Standard.E4.128 includes zero integrated local storage disks, requiring external cloud block volumes or remote network filesystems for data persistence. Additionally, the instance contains no GPU acceleration hardware, focusing its full operational envelope on general-purpose and memory-centric x86 execution.

With 2048.0 GB of RAM and 256 dedicated execution threads consolidated onto a single bare-metal host, the instance offers strong qualitative resource density for scale-up architectures, reducing inter-node networking overhead typical of distributed clusters. BM.Standard.E4.128 is suited for memory-intensive enterprise systems, large in-memory databases, demanding analytics workloads, continuous integration pipelines, and large-scale ETL data processing.
